Foreign politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and senior management approval in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12 and the AML/CFT Act 2018.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - International Companies Registry (name clearance executed through licensed registered agents and SIFA e-registry services)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in English or any language using the Latin alphabet; non-Latin script names must be rendered in a romanized transliteration. The liability indicator must be the English suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal, the licensed registered agent receives a formal rejection notice from the Registrar of International Companies. The applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar within 14 days, distinguishing the proposed name from conflicting registry entries. If reconsideration is denied, a formal administrative appeal may be lodged with the Minister responsible for the International Companies Act 1987 within 30 days of the denial; the Minister's decision is final, subject to judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as a substitute for the statutory registered office. The International Company must maintain a registered office in Samoa at the physical address of its licensed registered agent in Apia under section 83 of the International Companies Act 1987. A virtual office may supplement, but cannot replace, the statutory substance requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk for the company itself; moderate supervisory inspection risk at the registered agent level. The Central Bank of Samoa and the Financial Intelligence Unit conduct periodic on-site AML/CFT inspections of licensed registered agents; likelihood estimated at 5% for the company premises and 20-30% for the registered agent's office in the first operating year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies Amendment Act 2009 and related regulations; principally Part II and sections 5–16 on incorporation, registered office and registered agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) — International Companies Registry, Apia, Samoa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; an International Company must state its authorised and issued capital in the Memorandum, may issue shares at par or premium, and is not subject to any escrow account rule for capital funds.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: ORDERED, RESOLVED AND DECLARED as follows: (1) The subscriber shares in the Company be and are hereby allotted, subscribed and issued to the founding subscriber at par value, and the register of members shall be updated accordingly. (2) The registered office of the Company shall be established at the office of the duly licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and such registered agent is approved and retained. (3) The board appointments on the incorporation filings are ratified, and [name] is appointed Secretary. (4) The directors and officers are authorised to open bank accounts, execute agreements, appoint counsel and complete all filings necessary for lawful operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFSA International Companies Registry via a licensed Samoa registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a SIFSA-licensed registered agent to conduct a name search and, if required, submit a name reservation request. Verify that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing international company. Execute the registered agent appointment letter and obtain the registered agent's signed consent.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (Latin alphabet, may include English translation)
Registered agent appointment letter
Certificate of incorporation of registered agent (if requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on distinctiveness or similarity grounds, select from a list of alternative names and resubmit; the registry normally issues a decision within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Samoa registered agent acting on behalf of the subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles consistent with the International Companies Act 1987, including the principal object of developing and supplying video game kernel-level anti-cheat and integrity middleware. Specify the capital structure, registered office clause, registered agent clause, director and secretary details, and any express powers required for banking and contracting. Have the subscribers and proposed officers execute each signed page in compliance with notarisation or apostille requirements.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association
Certified copy of passport of each subscriber, director and secretary
Proof of residential address for each director and secretary
Consent to act as director and secretary
Power of attorney to the registered agent (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFSA or the registered agent identifies drafting defects, prepare an amendment to the Memorandum or Articles and obtain fresh signature pages before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Statutory Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFSA International Companies Registry, Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent electronically files Form IC-1 together with the executed Memorandum and Articles, the registered agent's consent, and the required director and secretary particulars. Pay the official government filing fee of USD 250 (or equivalent in Samoa tala) by bank transfer or card to the SIFSA designated account. Retain the payment receipt and the agent's submission acknowledgment.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered agent consent
Director and secretary consent and particulars
Government fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the registered agent has 14 days to file a corrective statement or revised documents; a re-filing fee may apply at SIFSA's published tariff.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry Examination and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: SIFSA verifies that the incorporation documents satisfy the International Companies Act 1987 and that the company is eligible for international company status and the related tax exemption. Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and a certified copy of the Memorandum and Articles. The registered agent collects the certificate and confirms the incorporation date and company number.
required_dossiers: Approved Form IC-1
Approved Memorandum and Articles
No further substantive dossiers at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses incorporation, the applicant may file a written appeal with SIFSA within 30 days, or the registered agent may cure any deficiency and file a fresh application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance Formalities and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and the licensed Samoa registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (physically or by written resolution) to adopt the pro-forma first board resolution covering share allotment, registered office adoption, officer appointments and bank account authorisations. Issue share certificates, maintain the register of members and other statutory registers, and deliver the Certificate of Incorporation, charter documents and board resolution to the chosen corporate bank for account opening.
required_dossiers: Pro forma first board resolution
Share certificates
Register of members, directors and secretary
Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Director and secretary passport copies and proofs of identity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a corporate record is defective, the board may ratify or correct it through a subsequent unanimous written resolution; no court filing is required for administrative corrections.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — the International Company is exempt from Samoan domestic licensing and tax licensing for its offshore video game anti-cheat software activities; no industry operating or manufacturing permit is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Government of Samoa — online Tax Administration System (TAS) portal: https://www.mfr.gov.ws. The Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), administers incorporation under the International Companies Act 1987, which is the mandatory prerequisite for tax registration of an International Company (IC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate the International Company with the Registrar of International Companies (MCIL) and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, and Certificate of Registered Office. Step 2 — Register with the Ministry for Revenue through the TAS portal (or paper lodgment at the MfR National Office, Apia) using Form TIN-AP, submitting the Certificate of Incorporation, registered office details, directors' and secretary particulars, and a certified copy of the IC's constitutional documents. Step 3 — Submit the statutory non-resident election under the International Companies Act and Income Tax Act 2015 to MfR to activate tax-exempt offshore treatment for the IC; obtain the TIN certificate and income tax registration number. Step 4 — Independently assess VAGST obligations: if the IC makes taxable supplies in Samoa exceeding SAT 80,000 per annum, lodge Form VAGST-REG with MfR; if the IC supplies only zero-rated exports (offshore cloud-delivered anti-cheat services), VAGST registration is not compulsory, but voluntary registration may be elected to recover input VAT on Samoan expenses. Step 5 — Open a Samoan commercial bank account and complete the Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) exchange control reporting forms to support future export proceeds repatriation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — A non-resident International Company is outside the Samoan income tax net: foreign-sourced revenue is exempt from income tax; no capital gains tax applies; no withholding tax is imposed on dividends, interest, or royalties paid to non-residents; and no annual company tax return is required for purely offshore operations. Entity_Level_Taxation — the IC is a corporate body; no pass-through or imputation regime applies to shareholders. Territorial_Scope — Samoan income tax applies only to residents and to Samoan-source income of non-residents; the IC neutralizes residence via statutory non-resident election. Pass_Through_Eligible — not applicable to this entity form.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Section 141 of the International Companies Act 1987 permits an IC to file a formal election with the Registrar and the Ministry for Revenue to be treated either as (i) an ordinary resident domestic company (subject to full Samoan taxation on worldwide income) or (ii) a non-resident/foreign company (tax-exempt on offshore profits). Absent such election, an IC is deemed to be a non-resident company. This election is the functional equivalent of a 'check-the-box' mechanism under Samoan law and does not trigger hybrid mismatch or CFC attribution. Samoa's Income Tax Act 2015 contains no separate hybrid mismatch elections, no REIT/trust pass-through elections relevant to ICs, and no branch-registered CFC elections. The election must be documented by board resolution and filed with both the Registrar and MfR; revocation is permitted upon proof of changed management and control.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) — Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2007, as amended, administered by the Ministry for Revenue (MfR).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT 80,000 (Samoan Tala) of annual taxable supplies made in Samoa (domestic taxable turnover). A foreign entity with no physical presence in Samoa is registrable only where it makes taxable supplies in Samoa; pure offshore export supplies — including cloud-delivered gaming anti-cheat licensing to non-resident studios — fall outside the Samoan supply rules and do not count toward the threshold. Voluntary registration may nonetheless be elected.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based e-invoicing clearance mandate is in force in Samoa. MfR operates a risk-based electronic filing and records-matching system through the TAS portal. Tax invoices must be sequential, issued within 28 days of supply, and contain: supplier legal name (or IC name), TIN and VAGST registration number, invoice date, description and quantity of supplies, consideration exclusive of VAGST, rate of tax, amount of tax payable, and total consideration. Records must be retained for at least 10 years under the Tax Administration Act 2012.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports are zero-rated under the VAGST Act 2007. Goods qualify if physically exported from Samoa within a reasonable period of the supply and supported by shipping evidence. Services qualify where the recipient is a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time of performance and the services are not consumed in Samoa. The Video Game Kernel-Level Anti-Cheat Engine, delivered as cloud-based software licenses and integrity middleware subscriptions to non-resident gaming studios, qualifies as a zero-rated export service where: (i) the customer is contractually domiciled and operating outside Samoa; (ii) the middleware is executed on servers located outside Samoa; (iii) the license is not made available for use to any Samoan-resident person; and (iv) payment is received in convertible foreign currency. The supplier must obtain and retain a signed non-residency declaration from each customer, a copy of the commercial license agreement, and technical usage logs or server deployment certificates evidencing offshore exploitation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Certified Copy of the Samoan Export Declaration (Customs) — required for any physical goods; for pure cloud-delivered middleware, a Service Export Declaration Form endorsed by MfR
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (for physical goods) / Offshore Server Deployment Certificate or cloud usage log (for digital services)
Original Commercial Invoice and executed Software License or SaaS Subscription Agreement with the non-resident customer
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or Foreign Currency Credit Advice issued by a Samoan commercial bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Customer Non-Residency Declaration and beneficial ownership identification (CBS exchange control format)
Proof of Aristocrat exemption — for hardware/software embedded components: customs import/export declarations aligned with HS 8471.50/8517.62 classifications, if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inward remittances for exports must be repatriated to Samoa within 180 days from the date of export or invoice (per Central Bank of Samoa exchange control policy); failure attracts CBS administrative penalties and forfeiture of foreign currency retention privileges. MfR subjects export VAGST refund claims to documentary pre-verification and risk-based post-clearance audit; incomplete customs declarations, bills of lading, or remittance certificates result in refund suspension and clawback. Fraudulent zero-rating claims attract: (i) reversal of the refund with interest at the statutory late payment rate; (ii) escalating civil shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 2012 — 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 50% for recklessness, and 150% for intentional evasion — calculated on the aggregate tax shortfall; (iii) criminal prosecution of the IC and its directors with fines up to 10,000 penalty units (SAT 1,000,000) and imprisonment for individuals of up to 3 years; and (iv) joint and several civil liability of directors and the registered agent. The audit window is 6 years, extended to 10 years for fraudulent or wilfully misleading claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Falefa, Apia, Samoa. CBS is the sole monetary authority, banking supervisor, exchange-control administrator and national payments-system overseer under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, the Exchange Control Act 1970, the Exchange Control Regulations 1971 and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2023. The Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit is the national FIU, and the Registrar of International and Foreign Companies within the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour administers the International Companies Act 1987 registry.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa holds IMF Article VIII status: current-account convertibility is free, so software license fees, royalties, subcontractor payments and registered-agent fees are payable offshore without CBS approval, subject only to bank-level documentary compliance (invoice, contract, purpose code). Capital-account transactions (equity injections, shareholder loans, capital reorganization) require CBS exchange-control approval or authorized-dealer no-objection if any WST conversion or a resident Samoan bank account is involved; USD-denominated injections into the International Company's external (non-resident) account bypass that perimeter because the IC is non-resident under the Exchange Control framework. Profit-remittance hurdles for resident Samoan companies are dividend withholding tax at the statutory rate and income-tax clearance before remittance; the IC is exempt from Samoan income tax and dividend withholding, so profit remittances are executed by board resolution from the external account with no Samoan tax leakage. The WST is on a CBS-managed currency-basket peg; IC treasury operations should be USD functional and WST conversion limited to local agent fees and government levies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Act 1970, Exchange Control Regulations 1971 and CBS Exchange Control Guideline No. 3 (Exports), export proceeds must be repatriated within 6 months of shipment (for services, within the contractually agreed settlement term) and offered to an authorized dealer within 30 days of receipt; 100% of receipts are to be surrendered into WST or, with CBS approval, held in a foreign-currency retention account. The International Company is a non-resident taxpayer and exchange-control person; receipts credited to its external USD account with an authorized dealer are not subject to WST surrender or any conversion ratio, and no exchange-control fee applies. If proceeds are accidentally routed into a resident WST account, the full surrender rule applies and a CBS retention approval is required to convert back into USD for offshore disbursement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-TO-MEDIUM as a primary banking rail, MEDIUM as a payout convenience. Wise, Revolut and Mercury do not accept Samoa-incorporated companies as account or merchant holders; Wise excludes Samoa from its supported registration list; Mercury is restricted to US LLCs; Revolut Business has no Samoa on-ramp. Payoneer may pay out to an IC's USD bank account but retains the Samoa IC in its restricted-configuration list. Airwallex has the broadest APAC-Pacific profile and may onboard a Samoa IC if the beneficial owners are clean-listed natural persons of Australia, New Zealand or Asia, but it will not issue a local clearing account in Samoa and requires full Certified Beneficial Ownership schedules. Legal constraint: the International Companies Act 1987 and Samoa AML/CFT law do not prohibit an IC from holding an offshore EMI account; the practical blocker is EMI jurisdictional policy and correspondent-bank de-risking. Recommended treasury architecture: the Samoa IC owns the anti-cheat IP and licenses publishers in USD; a US LLC or Singapore Pte operates the Stripe merchant account (Stripe does not underwrite a Samoa-incorporated merchant of record), sweeps the net processing proceeds weekly by SWIFT MT103 to the IC's BSP external account, and the IC executes contractor and cloud disbursements from that same regulated account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: De facto mandatory physical appearance of the principal Director and Company Secretary for an in-branch interview in Apia at BSP, SCB and NBS. The CBS risk-based CDD guidance allows fully remote onboarding only under enhanced due diligence, but no Samoan bank currently operates a zero-face-to-face IC program. BSP requires the principal Director to attend in person once; a second signatory may complete a notarized-power-of-attorney plus video attestation. SCB and NBS accept one director visit certified by a licensed Samoan registered agent, evolving to remote review for later signatories. Bank of Samoa has no documented IC remote route. Practical execution: the director attends Apia for one working day with original passport, proof of residential address, Certificate of Incorporation, the beneficial-ownership register required under the International Companies Act (as amended), board resolutions and a search-certificate of the register of charges; all backing documents may be couriered thereafter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 'Gaming' keyword trigger: underwriting and correspondent-bank screening engines map 'Gaming' and 'Anti-Cheat' transcripts to illegal-online-gambling typologies, casino software high-risk codes or exploit-tooling cybersecurity risk; 'Kernel-Level' terminology compounds the review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511 industry-classification confirmation letter from a licensed registered agent or audit firm; a two-page 'Not a Gambling Platform' compliance memorandum; an executed License Agreement naming the video-game studio or middleware distributor; the US-LLC/Stripe-to-IC payment flow diagram; a representation that no RNG, sweepstakes, slots, betting-exchange, crypto-gambling or casino-management counterparty exists; a console-platform or Unreal/Unity integration certificate demonstrating engine-level integrity; and, where not yet certified, an ISO 27001 or SOC 2 Type II remediation roadmap.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Samoa IC zero-tax offshore profile: no local staff, a PO Box address, and nominee-dense IC registry characteristics can be scored as a tax-transparent offshore legal arrangement or 'IP-holding shell', triggering automatic enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial-ownership register required under the International Companies Act (as amended) with passport copies of every natural-person UBO holding 10% or more; notarized trust deed or corporate-chart mapping if a holding layer intervenes; 24-month UBO bank statements evidencing source of funds and wealth; tax-residency certificates for all UBOs; the registered-agent engagement letter and fee receipts proving an active Samoan service relationship; annual-return and annual-license-fee receipts from the MCIL Registrar showing the IC is not dormant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance and going-concern challenge: no payroll, no office lease, no statutory audit and the absence of an economic-substance requirement for Samoa ICs can cause the bank or its USD correspondent to freeze the account pending a substance questionnaire.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance dossier comprising audited or compiled financial statements (voluntary under the IC Act but recommended), cloud-infrastructure hosting invoices for the anti-cheat backend, named third-party engineering subcontracts, trademark or patent registration certificates for the anti-cheat brand, board minutes appointing a compliance officer and authorizing IP commercialization, an annual operating budget, and an executed service or sales-channel agreement with the US LLC or Singapore Pte.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Return and Annual Licence Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% of the annual fee per month or part thereof; continued non-payment exceeding 90 days triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution of the International Company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority / Anti-Money Laundering Division, Central Bank of Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the company's incorporation and promptly upon any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A monetary penalty of WST 100 per day for each day of non-compliance; repeated failure may lead to administrative fines up to WST 10,000 and striker-off in conjunction with the Registrar of International Companies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Compliance Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually as part of the Annual Return, by the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a licensed registered agent in Samoa results in automatic administrative strike-off after 30 days' notice and revocation of the International Company's registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit for Samoa International Companies; an audit may be voluntarily appointed by shareholders or required under the company's articles of association, but there is no minimum revenue or asset threshold mandating an external audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa) as amended; International Companies are exempt from local taxation and are not required to file financial statements; where prepared voluntarily, accounts are typically prepared under IFRS or a recognized national GAAP acceptable to the directors.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must maintain a beneficial ownership register and file an annual confirmation with the Samoa International Finance Authority confirming the identity of all registrable beneficial owners. Shareholding transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members within 14 days, and the annual confirmation must be updated to reflect the transferee as the new registered beneficial owner before the anniversary deadline.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholder and Director Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 5,000 only if voluntarily audited; no statutory audit is required
